input_normalisation_note: NOT md-strip-v1. Cycle 5's encoder and structural features were both trained on raw text with markdown syntax intact (verified against train.py and the training data: the human-structured-govuk source and all 418 rows of the matched-eval-humans held-out set are 100% markdown-formatted in the raw text field). Feeding md-strip-v1 output to this model removes the structure the features exist to detect. See services/local-engine/research/cycle5-train/deploy-prep/PHASE1-PARITY-NOTE-2026-09-01.md.
features_contract_note: Three-input ONNX: input_ids, attention_mask, feats[8]. Feature order and z-normalisation are FEATURE_NAMES/FEATURE_NORM in opace-website/astro-latest/src/lib/content-integrity/features-v1.ts, copied verbatim from this file's own feature_norm block below (which is itself copied verbatim from ../models/tier3-cycle5-full-config.json, the packaged candidate's own config). A server-side Python equivalent does not exist yet (Phase 4).
scoring: MARGIN SPACE, not the calibrated-probability threshold shape tier3-cycle2-v1 used. The model's raw logit margin per segment (AI-logit minus human-logit, in logit units, NOT passed through softmax/temperature for the verdict decision) is m. flag <=> max(m1, m2 + secondary_gap) >= threshold, where m1/m2 are the top two segment margins. Temperature (1.0479) calibrates the DISPLAYED probability (softmax(logits/temperature)[1]) for score bands and copy, but the verdict itself is decided in margin space, per CYCLE5-REPORT's own method (cycle-4 lesson: the secondary must never be pinned to a probability ratio).
secondary_gap_note: ADDITIVE in margin space (m2 + 0.34), not a second probability cutoff. This replaces tier3-cycle2-v1's secondary_threshold field, which was a probability value (0.9763) compared directly. There is no cycle-5 equivalent probability secondary threshold; do not carry the field name across unchanged.
operating_point: a=3.570935 (quote 3.571), gap=0.34, in margin space, under segmentation contract segments-v3. Fitted against the shipped cycle-2 model's false-positive count on the long-form eval view (41/4,500 human documents, 0.9%): gap g swept 0.00-2.00 step 0.02, primary a solved exactly per gap to match the target FP count on the eval view's human documents, then (a,g) chosen to maximise AI detection. Split-half stability 0.34/0.26 (two random halves, seed 20260831). Full method, fresh reproduction and every figure's denominator: docs/measurements/CYCLE5-OPERATING-POINT-2026-08-31.md.
runtime_note: PENDING — cycle 5's WASM-vs-native-onnxruntime agreement (the tier3-cycle2-v1 runtime_note above) has not been separately re-measured for the int8 model under a real browser. The fp32-vs-int8 flip rate at the training checkpoint is measured (CYCLE5-REPORT gate 6: 0.19% flips on the full long-form set at export). The int8-vs-fp32 figures below are both measured on real onnxruntime (Python, native) scoring, not through onnxruntime-web/WASM in an actual browser — that measurement is Phase 4/5, matching tier3-cycle2-v1's own execution_provider_note discipline (WASM vs WebGPU were separately re-measured after the model shipped, not assumed from native scoring).
supersedes: tier3-cycle2-v1 (tier3-cycle2-e5small-int8-perchannel.onnx / -fp32.onnx), operating point 0.9855/0.9763 in probability space
